speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help identify the cause, can you describe exactly how the sensation feels and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Given your age and the specific description of position-dependent spinning, I suspect a displaced otoconial fragment in your inner ear. Do you have any associated symptoms like hearing loss in a specific ear, tinnitus, or difficulty walking that we should address?
